title: ProEtaleRingedPullbackUnderlyingOfUniverses
statement: Let f:X to Y be any morphism of schemes in universe t [def-pc-scheme], with their actual small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Fix an independent universe u and put r=max(u,t+1). Let L and B be left adjoints to actual sectionwise ring and abelian direct image at coefficient size r [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let R,S be ring sheaves of size r on Y and X, and c:R to f_*S a ring-sheaf map. Suppose its ring adjunct L(R) to S is invertible. Let P be any left adjoint to module direct image through c on the categories of module sheaves of size r [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then P followed by forgetting to abelian sheaves is naturally isomorphic to forgetting R-modules to abelian sheaves followed by B. This is valid for noncommutative ring sheaves as well, including the zero ring and empty schemes.

proof.text: Transport the ring and abelian adjunctions to the coefficient-sized AsSmall models using fully faithful restriction. The ring adjunct of the transported direct map is the inverse-equivalence image of the original adjunct and is invertible. Compare that adjunct with the canonical ring pullback by uniqueness of left adjoints. The unit equation and the generic forgetful-pullback comparison make this into a set inverse-image presentation of the target ring. This proves the presentation directly, without the fixed-universe pro-etale ring-presentation lemma.

Apply the generic inverse-image action/adjunction theorem to this ring presentation. Uniqueness of the small-site ring, module and abelian left adjoints gives the small-site underlying-sheaf comparison. Transport the canonical small module adjunction back along the module equivalences: the composite direct image is identified with actual pushforward through c by the sectionwise identity isomorphism. Compare its left adjoint with P. Finally whisker the small underlying comparison with the two equivalences and cancel their counits. This gives the displayed actual-site comparison, for arbitrary independent universes, including zero rings and empty schemes.

theorem proEtale_ringedPullback_underlying_of_isIso
    {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (L : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)} ⥤
      Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})
    (aL : L ⊣ (proEtaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      RingCat.{max u (t + 1)} (ProEt.topology Y) (ProEt.topology X))
    (B : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)} ⥤
      Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)})
    (aB : B ⊣ (proEtaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      AddCommGrpCat.{max u (t + 1)} (ProEt.topology Y) (ProEt.topology X))
    (R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology Y) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})
    (S : Sheaf (ProEt.topology X) RingCat.{max u (t + 1)})
    (c : R ⟶ ((proEtaleBaseChange f).sheafPushforwardContinuous
      RingCat.{max u (t + 1)} (ProEt.topology Y) (ProEt.topology X)).obj S)
    [IsIso ((aL.homEquiv R S).symm c)]
    (P : SheafOfModules.{max u (t + 1)} R ⥤ SheafOfModules.{max u (t + 1)} S)
    (aP : P ⊣ SheafOfModules.pushforward.{max u (t + 1)} c) :
    Nonempty (P ⋙ SheafOfModules.toSheaf S ≅ SheafOfModules.toSheaf R ⋙ B)
